reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lebanon facility in Warren County sits on 123 acres with 400,000 square feet of technical space and 12 MW of published IT capacity, making it the largest published facility in Ohio by power. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 12 MW of IT load translates to roughly 300 racks as an assumption. The campus comprises a single building matched directly to the operator's own specification.

The facility holds ISO 27001 certification for information security management and SOC 2 Type II certification for security, availability, and confidentiality controls, each addressing operational and compliance risk in production environments. The site supports colocation, production hosting, and disaster recovery services with a 24-hour staffed network operations center and build-to-suit deployment options.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 60.4 MW across the state. This single campus accounts for 19.9 percent of Ohio's published IT load, concentrating a significant share of the state's publicly disclosed hyperscale infrastructure in one location near Cincinnati.
